well: IODP Hole 362-U1480G - NORTH SUMATRA SUBDUCTION INPUTS, NE Indian Ocean / Wharton Basin (3.0343 N, 91.6056 E; seafloor -4,147.5 m), the sedimentary section that becomes the megathrust which ruptured in the 2004 Mw 9.2 Sumatra-Andaman earthquake; IODP Expedition 362 (2016), samples 1250.11-1359.76 mbsf - among the deepest sample depths in the catalogue's laboratory-mechanics family, from the pre-decollement horizon itself
operator_on_log: Stanislowski & Ikari (MARUM, ERC grant 714430 'Plate-rate experimental deformation') - direct-shear cohesion experiments on intact and powdered samples at ~in-situ stresses, with the archive's own calculated cohesion coefficient; the catalogue's FIFTH Ikari-lab entry, completing the subduction QUINTET (Nankai, Japan Trench, Hikurangi, Costa Rica, Sumatra); drilling by JOIDES Resolution
source_database: PANGAEA, dataset doi:10.1594/PANGAEA.966083 ('Cohesion experiment details and measurements of samples from IODP Hole 362-U1480G (Table 3)'), in bundle doi:10.1594/PANGAEA.966244; related to Stanislowski, Huepers, Fagereng & Ikari 2025, Geology 53(4), 360-364 (doi:10.1130/G52910.1) - 'Weak, frictionally unstable input sediments explain shallow seismogenesis at the north Sumatran subduction zone'; Enhanced curation
license: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC-BY-4.0), declared IN the file's own header and license-checked BEFORE cataloguing. Attribution: Stanislowski/Ikari / PANGAEA / IODP / ERC 714430
fetch_method: read-only HTTPS fetch of the PANGAEA textfile export - COMPLETE dataset (91 data points per the header's own Size declaration, re-counted EXACT at gate time: 13 rows x 6 full columns + 4 in-situ vertical stresses + 9 consolidation normal stresses, geocode excluded) in one fetch
coverage: COMPLETE DATASET: 13 direct-shear cohesion experiments - 4 intact + 9 powdered samples at effective stresses 10.71-14.03 MPa, cohesion 188-990 kPa, cohesion coefficient 0.014-0.082; four depths carry intact/powder replicate pairs
curves: Eff vert stress [MPa] (in-situ; intact rows only) / Eff normal stress [MPa] (consolidation; powder rows only) - proven complementary
Condition (intact/powder) verbatim; experiment IDs + IODP labels verbatim; the header's own note about italicized side-friction corrections preserved
source_anomaly_disclosure: No internal inconsistencies detected - the archive closes against its own definitions: the cohesion coefficient re-derives as C divided by the row's populated stress on ALL 13 rows within 0.0005 (rounding of the 3-decimal coefficient), and the identity itself REVEALS the table's structure - the two stress columns are perfectly complementary (intact rows carry only the calculated in-situ vertical stress, powder rows only the device consolidation stress; never both, never neither), which is also exactly what makes the 91-point Size declaration close; noted for the record: the header states that the printed version marks side-friction-corrected values in italics - formatting the plain-text export cannot carry, disclosed by the archive itself
purpose: forty-seventh catalogue entry - NORTH SUMATRA / WHARTON BASIN joins as region THIRTY-FOUR (the inputs to the deadliest megathrust of the century - the 2004 Mw 9.2 that killed ~230,000 people - drilled 1.25-1.36 km below the seabed at the horizon that becomes the decollement) and COHESION is kind THIRTY-SIX: the strength intercept that friction coefficients alone cannot give, the missing term of the Mohr-Coulomb envelope the catalogue's four friction kinds already span; the Geology headline is re-derived on every gate run: these sediments are WEAK - cohesion never exceeds 990 kPa at ~13 MPa stress, cohesion coefficients 0.014-0.082 (strength intercepts of 1.4-8.2 percent of the confining stress) - the weakness that let the 2004 rupture propagate shallow and generate its full tsunami
verified: 13 rows / 91 counted cells against the header's own Size declaration (EXACT, closing only through the proven stress-column complementarity); Ccoef = C/stress identity 13/13 within 0.0005; intact<->vertical and powder<->normal condition-stress coupling 13/13; cohesion range [188, 990] kPa and coefficient range [0.014, 0.082] pinned; four intact/powder replicate depths pinned; gate-pinned; source URL serves the identical dataset
